name: Christopher Wren
summary: English architect, astronomer, mathematician, and anatomist known for St. Paul's Cathedral and contributions to the Royal Society.

name: Charles Scarburgh
summary: English physician and anatomist who taught Wren and succeeded Harvey as Lumleian Lecturer.

name: Thomas Willis
summary: English physician and founding member of the Royal Society known for work on neurology and the Circle of Willis.

name: Robert Boyle
summary: Anglo-Irish natural philosopher and chemist known for Boyle's Law and foundational work in chemistry and physics.

name: William Harvey
summary: English physician who made seminal contributions in anatomy and physiology, particularly the circulation of blood.

name: John Wilkins
summary: English clergyman and natural philosopher, Warden of Wadham College and founder of the Royal Society.

name: Richard Lower
summary: English physician who performed the first blood transfusion and worked with Willis on neurology.

name: Robert Hooke
summary: English natural philosopher and architect known for Hooke's Law and Micrographia.

name: Wadham College
summary: Constituent college of the University of Oxford where Wren studied and Wilkins was Warden.

name: All Souls College
summary: Constituent college of the University of Oxford where Wren was a Fellow.

name: Royal Society
summary: Learned society for science founded in London in 1660, of which Wren was a founder and President.

name: Gresham College
summary: Institution of higher learning in London where Wren served as Professor of Astronomy.

name: Oxford University
summary: Collegiate research university in Oxford, England, where Wren studied and held professorships.

name: Westminster School
summary: Independent boarding school in London where Wren was educated before Oxford.

name: Cerebri Anatome
summary: 1664 anatomical work by Thomas Willis featuring illustrations by Christopher Wren.

aliases: Micrographia, or Physiological Descriptions of Minute Bodies
name: Micrographia
summary: 1665 book by Robert Hooke on microscopy, acknowledging Wren's pioneer work in the field.

name: Sheldonian Theatre
summary: Ceremonial hall of Oxford University designed by Christopher Wren.

name: Windsor
summary: Town in Berkshire, England, where Wren spent his childhood.

name: London
summary: Capital city of England, where Wren worked as Gresham Professor and built major structures.

name: Oxford
summary: City in Oxfordshire, England, home to the university where Wren studied and taught.
